new_senses.gloss: verbannen, ins Exil schicken (mit l- Ziel)
new_senses.rationale: Repeated finite nfewole/nfanwole occurs with human patients and Anatolia as l-destination, beside explicit nafi and paraphrases qəlʕiwole/mšayʕiwole lu nafi. First proposed entry; weak radical and base-form vocalism remain unestablished.

added_examples.turoyo: <...> W bəṯr l Atatürk manfaqle “nafi“, nfewole ġalabe mar rabe das səryoye. Kule nfanwole lu Anadol.
added_examples.translation: <...> And afterwards Atatürk issued 'nafi' [exile]; they had exiled many of the leaders of the Syriac Christians. They would exile all of them to Anatolia.
added_examples.rationale: First Preterit-wa attestation, with exile context and following Infectum-wa destination clause retained. English is the supplied project machine translation.

added_examples.turoyo: <...> nfewole ġalabe mar rabe das səryoye. Kule nfanwole lu Anadol.
added_examples.translation: <...> they had exiled many of the leaders of the Syriac Christians. They would exile all of them to Anatolia.
added_examples.rationale: First Infectum-wa attestation of the new entry; the preceding patient clause keeps Kule and the object suffix understandable. English is the supplied project machine translation.

added_examples.turoyo: Fayiši ḥamməš-šeṯ šne (5-6) bu nafi. Nfewole aṭ ṭaye w aṣ ṣəroye kulle, ar rabe, u ḥa d kətwo aʕle d miṣalewo aʕle, kulle qəlʕiwole lu nafi. <...>
added_examples.translation: They stayed five or six years in exile. They had exiled the Muslims and the Syriac Christians, all the leaders, whoever had something against him, against whom someone had informed; they would send them all into exile. <...>
added_examples.rationale: Second Preterit-wa example; a paraphrase with sending into exile independently anchors the proposed lexical meaning. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: Proposed new entry nfy, stem I, based on three tokens in two adjacent verses. They are repeated local evidence, not three independent sources.
Finite nfewole/nfanwole is distinct from nominal nafi. No separate light-verb idiom manfaqle nafi is added from this root assignment.
The difference between Preterit-wa and Infectum-wa is provisionally the reader's; unmarked singular Preterit/Infectum base forms and nfy versus nfw cannot be reconstructed securely from these forms.
Confirm nfy versus nfw, the unmarked Preterit/Infectum base forms, and segmentation/agent-object roles in nfewole and nfanwole.
